body:
## Summary

Fixes #2074.

- Detects explicitly requested Codex plugins and Agent Skills from the issue and its complete comment history before starting the solver.
- Provisions missing plugin providers into persistent, repository-scoped Codex state and verifies that each requirement is available.
- Reuses the scoped state in direct execution and mounts both Codex plugin state and standard Agent Skills in Docker isolation.
- Fails before the expensive harness starts with an actionable diagnostic when a requirement cannot be resolved.
- Documents the operator workflow, persistence behavior, experiments, timeline, requirements, research, and raw incident data.

## Root cause

The original task requested Superpowers from inside an already-created Codex session. That session could only suggest plugins included in its initial `recommended_plugins` list, while a fresh repository-scoped Codex home also lacked the marketplace snapshot checksum needed to resolve and install a provider. The task therefore failed before implementation even though the operator's existing Codex installation could provide the dependency.

## Reproduction

`tests/codex-capability-preflight.test.mjs` reproduces the missing-capability path with an isolated Codex home. Before the implementation, the preflight module was absent and the test failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The test now covers:

- dependency detection and curated-remote alias normalization;
- command-text false positives;
- existing standard Agent Skills;
- provider discovery, installation, verification, and persistence;
- refreshed operator authentication and installation identity;
- direct and Docker propagation;
- exact actionable failure diagnostics.

## Implementation

The preflight scans the issue title, body, and paginated comments for explicit plugin/skill requirements. It first checks standard user and project Agent Skill locations, then discovers providers from the operator's Codex marketplace catalog. Required plugins are installed into `$CODEX_HOME/hive-mind/repositories/<owner>/<repo>`, with current operator configuration and credentials refreshed on every run. The target checkout is not modified.

See the complete [issue 2074 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2074-055b34c0a946/docs/case-studies/issue-2074) for the incident timeline, acceptance mapping, research sources, experiments, and preserved raw data.

## Verification

- `node tests/codex-capability-preflight.test.mjs`
- live preflight against link-assistant/hive-mind#2074
- complete Node 24 default suite: all 328 selected test files passed
- ESLint
- Prettier
- documentation language and option synchronization
- MJS syntax and file line limits
- duplication threshold (10.61%)
- changeset validation

No screenshots are included because this is a non-visual solver/runtime change. Research found no Codex or Superpowers upstream defect requiring a separate report; the failure was in hive-mind's pre-session provisioning boundary.
title: Provision required Codex capabilities per repository (#2074)
